corrections.why: The Aermotor MC-39 was the 1934 tower. The tower standing since 1965 is a 54-foot steel tower with a CL-100 cab.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A hiker's blog gives 1959 for the present structure and 1925 for the first tower. The Register and the Forest Lookouts page both give 1965 for the present cab and tower, and the 1920s for the first wood tower. The record keeps 1965.

notes_for_editor: Build history is well sourced (Register, Forest Lookouts page and 2020 report agree on the 1965 cab and tower). The brief's 'Aermotor' design is corrected: the Aermotor MC-39 was the 1934 tower. Staffing 'when fire danger is high' rests on one hiker's undated blog post, cited as a tag page; no official staffing source found. The blog also says the landing was closed on that visit; the story advises checking before climbing and does not encourage it. Access status not established. Register elevation 8,137 ft (2,480 m); an OpenStreetMap tower node gives 2477 m; not used in the story. Height 16.5 m is the 54-foot tower converted (16.46 m). The 2020 report year comes from its title, 2020 Year-End Report. No photos added.
